summary: Keep the visibly non-neutral Tone recipe and its existing self-reference rule.
evidence: +0.55 EV changes linear gain to about 1.46 and +0.18 contrast changes the tonal slope; the Tone eye bypasses both. The OFF Exposure and Contrast probes are already explicitly skipped at line 851; both Denoise probes still run.
proposed_fix: Keep Exposure +0.55 EV and Contrast +0.18 on IMG_7723.CR3 and DSC00636.ARW; keep the skips unchanged.
check: Phase 3 Tone ON/OFF pixel signature and both Denoise probe pairs; only ON has timed Tone impacts.

summary: Keep an explicitly authored 0 EV Exposure Band and select it before the own probe.
evidence: Default positions are [-6,-3,0,3,6]. seed clones the nodes and adds +0.8 EV to the midpoint. This yields about 1.74x gain at the authored band and a nonzero correction in neighboring tones. Selection defaults to index 2 but lives in shared UI state; ownControls already remaps to the SDR slider when requested.
proposed_fix: Keep node pairs [[-6,0],[-3,0],[0,0.80],[3,0],[6,0]] as [input_ev,adjustment_ev] on IMG_7723.CR3 and DSC00636.ARW; use default smoothing 0.5 and explicitly select index 2 before own timing.
check: Compare ON/OFF signatures and assert the 0 EV band changed during the own slider drag.

summary: The luma seed bends the curve, but the own probe guesses the handle location without using the plot insets.
evidence: An authored mid-node at [0.5,0.58] bends the normalized luma mapping. canvasDrag clicks at 42% of the full canvas height; curveEditorLayout uses top=14 and bottom=34, so the pointer can miss the handle or hit another part of the curve.
proposed_fix: Keep luma [[0,0],[0.25,0.19],[0.5,0.58],[0.75,0.83],[1,1]] on IMG_7723.CR3 and DSC00636.ARW; use the editor's logical plot transform on [0.5,0.58] for the drag start.
check: Check ON/OFF signatures and assert an actual change to the seeded mid-point on own.curves.curve.drag.

summary: The Highlight Compression seed raises peak levels but the harness does not check that the cap was exercised.
evidence: Exposure +3 EV multiplies input by eight and the eye leaves Exposure alone, so 600 nits requires more than 75 nits before the boost if the rest of the pipeline is neutral. A compositor hash can differ from shoulder changes alone and does not verify that the bypassed image exceeded target.
proposed_fix: Use IMG_7723.CR3 and DSC00636.ARW with Exposure +3 EV in both states, Peak Fit / maximum, HDR target 600 nits and Start 200 nits (on the native 25-nit grid). For explicit SDR runs use Peak Fit / maximum and Start 55%. Confirm HDR OFF pre-limiter BT.2020 channel peak >600 nits and ON maximum finished BT.2020 channel <=600 nits before accepting the row.
check: Phase 3 Highlight Compression eye/impact signatures plus pre-limiter HDR peak and exact finished ceiling checks.

summary: Every native Tone input redraws both highlight graphs and runs unrelated global panel bookkeeping before scheduling a frame.
evidence: app-boot.js input listener calls commitAdjustmentValue synchronously. renderControlState walks all rows and groups, calls HSL and Film UI renderers, and renders both highlight plots with 161 curve samples apiece; only GPU rendering is coalesced.
felt_impact: Unmeasured estimate: roughly 5–20 ms of whole first feedback at Fit under dense events, or one missed frame; settle likely little changed.
proposed_fix: Keep slider value/readout synchronous; batch dependent graph and badge updates once per animation frame, flush final values on release, and leave preview invalidation semantics unchanged.
check: Audit own Tone Exposure/Contrast and all impact Tone probes; sample time in input handlers and compare first feedback and settle.

summary: Direct SDR Peak Fit brackets a GPU-to-CPU peak readback around each eligible frame, including live draws when liveMode is set.
evidence: finishedSdrAnchor requires direct SDR and Peak Fit with an automatic anchor; settled frames qualify even with a canonical cache entry. renderToFrame submits the graph, reduces the entire finish texture into a frame-serial cache entry, awaits mapAsync, deletes the entry, then resumes presentation. Interactive frames only take this route when frameAnchor or liveMode is active.
felt_impact: Unmeasured estimate for an eligible cache hit: roughly 10–40 ms Fit or 30–100 ms at larger Direct sizes out of the whole feedback/settle wait; no expected gain for normal HDR drag.
proposed_fix: First measure the eligible route. Reuse an identical finished-signal peak where graph inputs, route/mip and signal selection match; otherwise keep first feedback independent only if the existing interactive image contract is preserved.
check: Run --lane sdr Highlight Compression and Tone impact probes, log liveMode, frameAnchor, execution mode and mapAsync timing; compare first feedback/settle and validate SDR parity.
notes: liveMode is set by the Library renderer; Grade typically takes this path for settled not interactive Direct SDR frames.

summary: A warm reduced Clean Grain delta can still be blended up front on every Tone frame.
evidence: The reduction key does not include Tone; when ensureFineGrainReduced returns cleanGrainDelta, renderToFrame allocates and submits another Fit blend before the grade, then retires it in finally, even when only Exposure or Contrast changed.
felt_impact: Unmeasured estimate: roughly 5–25 ms of whole Fit first feedback with a qualifying warm Clean Grain setup; otherwise zero.
proposed_fix: Retain one allocator-budgeted resolved blend keyed by the reduced texture identity plus colorSplotches strength; invalidate on source/mip/control change.
check: Compare tone.exposure and tone.contrast in a supplemental warm Clean Grain ON repeat; H1's isolated slide and Denoise toggle steps alone do not test this combined state. Count Fit blend dispatches and compare GPU-fenced first feedback.

summary: Moving an already-active global curve can reuse Detail's sharpen bands from the previous curve on the tiled route.
evidence: detailBandIdentity hashes serialized parameter slots and proxy identity. Curve point values live in a separate LUT buffer; moving a point with the same enabled-channel bits does not alter this key. encodeTiledGeneration runs the new base shader, then reuses packed Detail bands from the old base when packed.hit and halo assembly succeed.
proposed_fix: Key packed global Detail bands by the effective global curve points/LUT identity as well as the upstream params; preserve reuse when the curve is unchanged.
check: At 100% force Tiled, enable global Sharpen/Texture, prime an active luma curve, move its existing point, and compare to the same grade after a cold tile-cache reset and CPU within tolerance.

summary: A Highlight Compression Start drag reruns the upstream picture graph and invalidates Peak Fit measurements even though Start is applied at the output.
evidence: Direct render unconditionally draws base through Detail/locals/Film before final composite; Tiled also emits the base graph. highlightAnchorRequest hashes the whole lane, including Start and shoulder-only settings. On a cache miss the HDR scheduler may render native analysis patches and redraw after release. HDR Target itself is not always tail-only because global Tone Whites uses it.
felt_impact: Unmeasured estimate at Fit: tens of milliseconds (roughly 15–60 ms) of first feedback if finishing alone can run; can also remove one background native anchor pass and redraw from settle/drain on unchanged input.
proposed_fix: Measure first; start with the Start slider and other proven tail-only controls. Reuse the pre-limiter finish texture and a peak key derived only from upstream inputs and selected signal, scoped to source/route/mip/current viewport and budget. Keep Tone-coupled targets in the upstream key when required.
check: Phase 3 own Highlight Compression Start drag with peak dispatch/count and all three clocks; supplement with Film/Detail enabled, and compare settled pixels/ceiling on both render routes.

summary: Exposure Bands reconstructs the same interpolation data up to 180 times per slider input and refreshes unrelated controls.
evidence: Each graph sample calls sampleToneEqualizerAdjustment, which normalizes and sorts the nodes again and recreates targets, widths, deltas and slopes. setToneEqualizerBand also calls syncControlsFromState on every input and drawToneEqualizerEditor syncs the band controls again.
felt_impact: Unmeasured estimate of roughly 3–15 ms of whole first feedback under dense input, most likely noticeable with many bands or if the old handler misses one frame.
proposed_fix: Prepare interpolation coefficients once per graph redraw and coalesce the graph and dependent control refresh to one frame, keeping the final slider state synchronous.
check: Phase 3 own.bands band-value drag plus a 16-node supplemental case; compare input-handler CPU time and whole first feedback and check rendered curve samples are identical.

summary: Unchanged global samples are already cached, but any authored local curve forces fresh packed allocation and LUT upload on every render.
evidence: buildCurves memoizes channel samples and the packed global array. uploadParamsAndCurves concatenates all non-neutral local curves into a new Float32Array and Map, which defeats its own reference-equality upload skip. Separately curve-editor.js renders and resamples the 96-point graph synchronously on each pointermove, while the preview LUT itself is sampled on rendered frames.
felt_impact: Unmeasured estimate: typically 1–5 ms of whole first feedback, potentially more with many curved locals; no global LUT resampling gain on a Tone drag with unchanged curves.
proposed_fix: Cache packed local/global storage and offsets by ordered IDs and sample identities. Repaint the graph at most once per frame with a final flush, retaining the existing per-channel sampler.
check: Phase 3 own.curves curve drag with input events versus graph redraws; supplement Tone Exposure drag with several curved locals, count uploads and compare first feedback.

summary: The default Peak Fit preset schedules an own-control drag on the hidden Softness slider, which can stop the module before its impact probes.
evidence: RANGE schedules both Start and Softness. Default mode is Peak Fit, and app code hides Softness unless mode is soft_ceiling. reveal expands collapsible ancestors but cannot clear the mode-specific hidden attribute, and a failed sample is rethrown at line 769. The generic Start drag also moves by 18% of the full 100–4000 nit range, which can cross the 600-nit target and move it indirectly.
proposed_fix: Use Peak Fit Start and Detail (not Softness) for this recipe, with a bounded HDR Start gesture such as 200 to 300 nits so Target stays at 600. If Softness needs timing, use a separately identified Soft Ceiling recipe.
check: Run a one-sample Highlight Compression calibration and check both own controls, eye and impact rows finish with HDR target unchanged during the own Start probe.

summary: The normal HDR Maximum anchor path can grow its peak cache without the 32-entry limit used by the compute path.
evidence: Bounded maximum analysis writes peakReductionCache directly at 1688 and the non-patch tiled path also writes directly at 2816. Only runPeakReduction caps that map at 32 (9923–9924). Maximum HDR is the default and does not need the compute path. Keys contain serialized lane and local recipes, so a long session with many settled edits retains old strings until session reset.
proposed_fix: Centralize all entries behind the same bounded insertion helper and retain the existing key/measurement semantics.
check: Use a lightweight cache test for more than 32 distinct Maximum keys, verify latest entries are retained and session reset still clears the cache.

summary: CPU and WGSL take different color paths for signed HDR pixels in a frame whose delivery channels are already below target.
evidence: CPU takes a frame-level all-below shortcut and clamps negative ACEScg channels. WGSL always converts to BT.2020, clamps every BT.2020 channel then round-trips. These operations are not equivalent on signed colors, even without highlight overshoot. The CPU and GPU both separately enforce the ceiling.
proposed_fix: First check signed, saturated low-brightness colors against the existing perceptual tolerances; if outside, align handling without changing the exact ceiling or weakening any limit.
check: Add a signed RAW or synthetic saturated sub-target fixture to existing HDR CPU/GPU agreement, test a just-over-target companion and use exact finished and existing encoded ceiling checks.
notes: Branch difference is confirmed statically; no observed perceptual tolerance failure or ceiling breach. Phase 2 findings-only; no patch produced.
